title: Model
description: Contract 3, the model contract: what a model adapter declares about what it can compute before a call, what a completion reports it used, and the price table money is computed with. The dialect on the wire is the chat-completions dialect most endpoints answer; this schema fixes what the core relies on beyond the dialect. See README.md.

Calculability.title: Calculability
Calculability.description: What an adapter can say about a call before it is made, and how its provider bills. Taktus derives from it which budget it can enforce and says so when a budget is set (ADR-0005, third amendment). An adapter declares no more than its provider permits; docs/research holds the evidence a declaration rests on.

input_count.description: How the adapter counts a prompt's input tokens before the call. exact: the count equals what the provider bills. upper_bound: the count is never below what the provider bills. estimate: the count may lie on either side. none: the adapter cannot count.

output_cap.description: Whether the output limit a call sets holds. hard: the provider never produces more output than the limit, reasoning included. soft: a limit exists but reasoning or tool output may lie outside it. none: output is unbounded.

usage_kinds.description: The price kinds the provider reports per call after it: input (uncached), output, cache_read, cache_write. Money is recomputable exactly only from kinds that are reported.

billing.description: How the provider bills. per_token: each call by its tokens. per_window: a share of a time window of a subscription; money is not a function of tokens. per_hardware_time: the time of hardware the operator owns or rents.

provider_limit.description: What the provider itself enforces over a longer period, as information: hard (requests are refused beyond it), alert (only a notice), none, unknown. Taktus never relies on it.

evidence.description: Where the declaration's evidence is written down, with its date.

PriceTable.title: PriceTable
PriceTable.description: One version of the prices money is computed with. A version is never changed once used: a new price is a new version, and the ledger names the version (by its digest) a run was converted at, so that money stays recomputable from the ledger (ADR-0010). A price is per unit_tokens tokens of one price kind of one model; a kind without a price is unpriced, and a cost that needs it says so instead of counting it as zero.

source.description: Where the prices were read, and when.

Exchange.title: Exchange
Exchange.description: One call as the conformance suite observed it: the declaration, what the adapter counted before the call, the output limit the call set, and the usage the provider reported after it. The checks M-02 to M-04 are rules over an exchange (src/taktus/conformance/model/rules.py); a schema cannot express them, so their must-fail fixtures are schema-valid.

counted.description: The adapter's count of the input before the call; absent when it declares none.

Usage.title: Usage
Usage.description: What one completion used, as the adapter reports it to the core: the totals, and the split by price kind of the one model that answered.
